title: Supported division for arbitrary finite formal divisors
statement: Let $L$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $n,s\ge0$, and let $G_1,\ldots,G_s$ be nonzero elements of $L[[T_1,\ldots,T_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Order exponents by ascending lexicographic order of $(|\alpha|,\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)$, and let $\alpha_i$ be the least exponent with nonzero coefficient in $G_i$. Put $E_i=(\alpha_i+\mathbf N^n)\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}(\alpha_j+\mathbf N^n)$, $\Delta_i=\{\beta:\alpha_i+\beta\in E_i\}$ and $E_0=\mathbf N^n\setminus\bigcup_i E_i$. For every $F\in L[[T_1,\ldots,T_n]]$ there exist unique $Q_1,\ldots,Q_s,R$ in that ring satisfying $F=\sum_i Q_iG_i+R$, $\operatorname{supp}Q_i\subseteq\Delta_i$, and $\operatorname{supp}R\subseteq E_0$. The support of a series is the set of its exponents with nonzero coefficient. If $F$ has no term of total degree less than $q$, then $R$ has none either, and $Q_i$ has no term of total degree less than $q-|\alpha_i|$ whenever this bound is positive. For $s=0$ the conclusion is $R=F$.

proof.text:
Write $\mu\prec
u$ for the order in the statement. The exponents of total degree at most $d$ form a finite set: each coordinate lies between $0$ and $d$. Thus each exponent has finitely many predecessors. Every nonempty set of exponents has a least element: first minimize total degree in $\mathbf N$, then choose the lexicographically least element of that finite degree. Translation preserves strict order: $\mu\prec
u$ implies $\mu+ eta\prec
u+ eta$, since either the total degrees differ or the first differing coordinate remains the same. These arguments include $n=0$.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, for the historical BM route only; the following coefficient proof is written by Q88, not quoted from this document. BM 1997, Theorem 3.17 and Remark 3.18, remains WANTED. Agent proof, step 1.

proof.text: The sets $E_0,E_1,\ldots,E_s$ are pairwise disjoint and cover $\mathbf N^n$. Indeed, an exponent in some orthant belongs to the first orthant containing it; all other exponents belong to $E_0$. If $\mu\in E_i$, the unique componentwise difference $\beta=\mu-\alpha_i$ lies in $\Delta_i$, and conversely $\beta\in\Delta_i$ gives $\mu=\alpha_i+\beta\in E_i$. Consequently there is exactly one slot for each exponent: a remainder slot for $\mu\in E_0$ or an $(i,\beta)$ quotient slot. This holds even if some $E_i$ are empty or some $\alpha_i$ coincide.

At the first exponent the sum is empty, and at every subsequent exponent all scalars on the right have already been assigned. This is ordinary recursion on the degree, with finite recursion inside each degree, and defines exactly one scalar at every exponent. Induction in this same order shows that any family obeying the formula equals this one.

u$. Terms with $ eta

proof.text:
For any other supported expression $F=\sum_i Q'_iG_i+R'$, encode its coefficients in slots: set $b_\mu=[T^\mu]R'$ on $E_0$ and $b_{\alpha_i+ eta}=c_i[T^ eta]Q'_i$ on $E_i$. The convolution computation in Step 5, using [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], gives $f_
u=b_
u+\sum_{\mu\prec
u}b_\mu[T^
u]C_\mu$. Thus $b$ obeys the recursion of Step 4 and equals $a$ by induction. On each quotient slot division by $c_i
e0$ is valid by [def-weil-field], so all coefficients of $Q'_i$ equal those of $Q_i$; the supports force the other coefficients to be zero. The same argument gives $R'=R$. This proves uniqueness without assuming the $G_i$ are a standard basis or generators of any specified ideal.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, for the historical BM route only; the following coefficient proof is written by Q88, not quoted from this document. BM 1997, Theorem 3.17 and Remark 3.18, remains WANTED. Agent proof, step 7.

proof.text:
Suppose $f_
u=0$ whenever $|
u|<q$. Induct in the recursion order over those exponents. Every predecessor $\mu\prec
u$ has $|\mu|\le|
u|<q$, hence its scalar is zero by the induction hypothesis. The displayed formula therefore gives $a_
u=0$. The coefficients of $R$ below degree $q$ vanish. If $| eta|<q-|\alpha_i|$, then $|\alpha_i+ eta|<q$; on a quotient slot its coefficient is $c_i^{-1}a_{\alpha_i+ eta}=0$, and off its slots it was defined to be zero. This gives exactly the asserted positive quotient bound.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, for the historical BM route only; the following coefficient proof is written by Q88, not quoted from this document. BM 1997, Theorem 3.17 and Remark 3.18, remains WANTED. Agent proof, step 8.

proof.text: If $s=0$, every slot is a remainder slot and $C_\mu=T^\mu$. The recursion then reads $a_\nu=f_\nu$, so $R=F$. If $n=0$, there is only the empty exponent: for $s>0$ the first orthant occupies it and all later $E_i$ are empty. The formulas give $Q_1=F/G_1$, $Q_i=0$ for $i>1$, and $R=0$; each $G_i$ is a nonzero scalar. For arbitrary $n$, an empty $E_i$ similarly forces $Q_i=0$. These verify the empty-variable, scalar-unit and repeated-initial-exponent cases directly.
